title: Introduction to Chemical Nomenclature
description: Learn the basics of naming chemical compounds and understanding chemical formulas.
content:
Chemical nomenclature is the system of naming chemical compounds. The rules for naming compounds are based on the type of compound and its chemical structure.

In this module, we'll focus on naming simple binary compounds - those composed of just two elements. These include:

1. Binary ionic compounds (metal + non-metal)
2. Binary molecular compounds (non-metal + non-metal)

For binary ionic compounds, we name the metal first (keeping its name unchanged), followed by the non-metal with its ending changed to '-ide'.

Examples:
- NaCl: sodium chloride
- MgO: magnesium oxide
- CaF2: calcium fluoride

For transition metals that can form multiple ions with different charges, we specify the charge using Roman numerals in parentheses.

Examples:
- FeCl2: iron(II) chloride
- FeCl3: iron(III) chloride
objectives: Identify the difference between ionic and molecular compounds
Understand how to indicate charges for transition metals
Recognize common chemical formulas and their names
